title: Dipolar-driven mean-field criticality in the ferrimagnet Eu$_2$MnSi$_2$O$_7$
authors: Masahiro Kawamata, Maxim Avdeev, Yusuke Nambu
abstract: We report mean-field critical behavior in Eu$_2$MnSi$_2$O$_7$, a melilite-type ferrimagnet with spin-only Eu$^{2+}$ and Mn$^{2+}$ moments and negligible orbital contributions. Magnetization measurements combined with neutron powder diffraction reveal critical exponents close to the mean-field values, indicating that long-range dipolar interactions govern the asymptotic critical behavior in this insulating ferrimagnet. The refined magnetic structure, described by the magnetic space group $P2_12_1^\prime2^\prime$, exhibits a tilted ferrimagnetic configuration driven by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, reflecting the noncentrosymmetric nature of the lattice. These results extend the applicability of mean-field theory to complex insulating magnets and establish Eu$_2$MnSi$_2$O$_7$ as a platform for exploring ferrimagnetism and long-range interactions. To our knowledge, this is the first insulating ferrimagnet in which dipolar interactions drive mean-field criticality.
summary: This study investigates the critical behavior of the ferrimagnet $	ext{Eu}_2	ext{MnSi}_2	ext{O}_7$, demonstrating that its magnetic ordering transition is governed by long-range dipolar interactions. By measuring magnetization and performing neutron diffraction, the authors confirm mean-field critical exponents, establishing this material as a key platform for studying dipolar criticality in insulating magnets.
main_problem: To establish mean-field critical behavior driven by long-range dipolar interactions in an insulating ferrimagnet, extending previous findings limited to ferromagnets.
main_result: The material exhibits mean-field critical exponents ($ eta \approx 0.42$, $\gamma \approx 0.9$) confirming that long-range magnetic dipole-dipole interactions govern the asymptotic critical behavior in this ferrimagnet.
method: Magnetization measurements, neutron powder diffraction (NPD), and analysis of critical exponents using scaling laws (e.g., Kouvel-Fisher plots).
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Eu}_2	ext{MnSi}_2	ext{O}_7$, a melilite-type ferrimagnet with spin-only Eu$^{2+}$ and Mn$^{2+}$ moments. The critical behavior is modeled by considering the long-range magnetic dipole-dipole (MDD) interactions.
key_observables: Critical exponents ($ eta, \gamma$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), magnetization ($M$), and magnetic reflection intensities from NPD.
important_parameters: The system operates in a regime where MDD interactions dominate the critical fluctuations, leading to mean-field universality class behavior.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that dipolar interactions are the dominant long-range force controlling the asymptotic critical exponents, despite the presence of exchange interactions stabilizing the order.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of susceptibility ($\chi$), NPD data comparing 3 K and 20 K reflections, and plots used to extract critical exponents using scaling analysis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures magnetic properties across temperatures, analyzes structural refinement via NPD to determine the magnetic space group ($P2_12'12'$), and then applies various thermodynamic/critical analyses (Arrott plot, scaling) to confirm mean-field critical exponents governed by dipolar interactions.
why_interesting: The confirmation of mean-field criticality in a complex insulating ferrimagnet provides an experimental realization for testing universality classes beyond simple ferromagnets, which is relevant for understanding phase transitions in many interacting quantum systems.

Magnetic noise spectroscopy.note: The study's core finding is the determination of mean-field critical exponents ($\eta, \gamma$) governing magnetic fluctuations near a phase transition, which directly relates to modeling fluctuation-dissipation relations linking noise to spin susceptibility.
